To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel bioinformatics pipeline was established to predict surface-associated proteins and its application was used to identify a set of potential diagnostic targets for Burkholderia pseudmallei.
a bioinformatic method has been developed for the identification of potential diagnostic targets and applied to a test dataset.

(i) the bioinformatic pipeline developed in this study can be used to rapidly identify potential targets for the development of new diagnostic assays for Burkholderia pseudomalie; and (ii) this pipeline can be applied to whole genome analyses in order to identify potential targets for development for new diagnostic assays for any bacterial species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bioinformatic methods and their application in the discovery of novel diagnostic targets.
the application of computational techniques to identify proteins which can be exploited as diagnostic reagents for Burkholderia.
the application of bioinformatics to the development of novel diagnostics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the methodology described in this thesis has the potential to be a valuable bioinformatics tool in the development of novel reagents for the diagnosis of infections arising from Burkholderia species and other pathogenic organisms.

a combination of in silico and wet lab approaches can provide a valuable and efficient method of selecting potential protein targets for the development of novel diagnostic reagents for the identification of B. pseudomallelia and related species.
the bioinformatic approach presented here is capable of identifying a set of potential diagnostic target proteins from B. pseudomallee.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have established a bioinformatics pipeline which can be used to predict surface-associated and secret proteins from any organism and we have demonstrated its application to B. pseudomallelai, the causative agent of melioidosis.
we have demonstrated a bioinformatic approach to the identification of diagnostic targets from the genome sequence of a pathogen.

we have established a bioinformatic framework which can be used to predict potential diagnostic targets and which can be used in the future as a rapid means of identifying novel diagnostic targets from the genomes of pathogenic organisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bioinformatics is a useful and efficient tool for predicting protein secretion and surface localization and can help to guide the development of diagnostic tools.
a bioinformatic approach can be used to identify proteins that are secreted or surface associated and thus potential targets for diagnostic assays.
the combination of bioinformatics and experimental approaches can provide a powerful method for the identification of potential diagnostic markers for pathogenic species of the genus Burkholderia.
